'''''Caladium bicolor''''', called '''Heart of Jesus''', is a species in the genus ''[[Caladium]]'' from Latin America. It is grown as a [[houseplant]] for its large, heart or lance-shaped leaves with striking green, white, pink, and red blotching. Hundreds of cultivars are available. (See [[List of Caladium cultivars]].) It can be planted outside in [[USDA Hardiness Zone]] 10 as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental]]. It is a problematic invasive species in [[Trinidad and Tobago]], [[Guam]], [[Micronesia]], [[Palau]], [[Hawaii]] and [[Philippines|the Philippines]], and naturalized populations can be found in most of the rest of the world's tropics, including [[Africa]], the [[Indian subcontinent]], southeast Asia and [[Malesia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cabi.org/ISC/datasheet/121808 |title=Caladium bicolor (heart of Jesus) |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=8 June 2020 |website=Invasive Species Compendium |publisher=CAB International |access-date=8 June 2020 }}</ref>

== Toxicity ==
''C. bicolor'' contains [[calcium oxalate]] crystals, making all parts of the plant poisonous to humans, livestock, and pets. Sap coming in contact with the skin may cause skin irritation. Ingestion may cause burning and swelling of the lips, mouth, and tongue, as well as nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Caladium bicolor (Angel Wings, Caladium, Candidum, Elephant's Ears, Exposition, Fancy-leaved Caladium, Malanga, Mother-in-law Plant, Pai, Pink Cloud, Stoplight, Taro, Texas Wonder, Via, Via sori) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/caladium-bicolor/|access-date=2021-02-18|website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title= Angel’s wings (Caladium) |url= https://www.childrens.health.qld.gov.au/poisonous-plant-angels-wings-caladium/ |access-date=18 February 2021 |publisher= Children’s Health Queensland Hospital and Health Service }}</ref> If a pet consumes caladium, in addition to vomiting, etc., the symptoms include drooling, pawing at mouth or face, and decreased appetite.<ref>{{cite web |title=Caladium |url= https://www.petpoisonhelpline.com/poison/caladium/ |work= Pet poison helpline |access-date=18 February 2021 }}</ref>
